title: Selective Formation of Chromogen I from N-Acetyl-D-glucosamine upon Lanthanide Coordination

list_of_rare_earth_compounds.compound_name: nonanuclear gadolinium oxo/hydroxo cluster with doubly deprotonated Chromogen I
list_of_rare_earth_compounds.formula: [Gd9(μ4-O)(μ3-OH)8(LH)4(OAc)4(H2O)12]·5ClO4·24H2O (LH = doubly deprotonated Chromogen I, C8H11NO5; elemental Gd9C40H136N4O93Cl5)

material_class.structural_family: nonanuclear Ln9 oxo/hydroxo cluster built on a square-pyramidal [Ln5(μ4-O)(μ3-OH)4] core; six clusters hydrogen-bond into a 54-metal cage

synthesis.procedure: Aqueous Gd(ClO4)3 (1.0 mol L−1) was prepared by dissolving gadolinium oxide (0.125 mol, 45.313 g) in aqueous perchloric acid (70.0–72.0%, 64.0 mL) at about 80 °C and diluting to 250.00 mL. Sodium acetate (273.0 mg, 2.0 mmol), N-acetyl-D-glucosamine (221.0 mg, 1.0 mmol), and Gd(ClO4)3 (4.0 mL, 4.0 mmol) were added to anhydrous ethanol (10 mL) and deionized water (5 mL). The solution was heated to about 80 °C, and aqueous NaOH (1.0 M) was added dropwise to the point of incipient but permanent precipitation. The mixture was refluxed for 2 h, filtered, and the filtrate was evaporated under ambient conditions to give pale-yellow block crystals after one week.

reagents.name: sodium hydroxide
reagents.amount: aqueous 1.0 M, dropwise to incipient permanent precipitation

synthesis.time: 2 h reflux; crystals after one week
synthesis.vessel_or_method: open reflux in ethanol/water followed by ambient evaporation
synthesis.workup_and_crystallization: Filtered; filtrate evaporated under ambient conditions to afford pale-yellow block crystals after one week.

properties.summary: χMT for nine Gd(III) ions falls from 68.61 cm3 K mol−1 at 300 K to 62.00 cm3 K mol−1 at 24 K and 31.16 cm3 K mol−1 at 2 K under 1000 Oe, indicating weak antiferromagnetic interactions. The magnetocaloric effect is ΔSm = 31.3 J kg−1 K−1 at 2 K and ΔH = 7 T, below the 18.7R limit for nine uncorrelated Gd3+ ions. CD spectra in EtOH are shown but no numerical chiroptical or luminescence data are reported.

measurements.name: calculated χMT for nine uncoupled Gd3+

list_of_rare_earth_compounds.compound_name: nonanuclear dysprosium oxo/hydroxo cluster with doubly deprotonated Chromogen I
list_of_rare_earth_compounds.formula: [Dy9(μ4-O)(μ3-OH)8(LH)4(OAc)4(H2O)12]·5ClO4·24H2O (LH = doubly deprotonated Chromogen I, C8H11NO5; elemental Dy9C40H136N4O93Cl5)

material_class.structural_family: nonanuclear Ln9 oxo/hydroxo cluster built on a square-pyramidal [Ln5(μ4-O)(μ3-OH)4] core; isostructural with the Gd analogue

synthesis.procedure: Aqueous Dy(ClO4)3 (1.0 mol L−1) was prepared by dissolving dysprosium oxide (0.125 mol, 46.625 g) in aqueous perchloric acid (70.0–72.0%, 64.0 mL) at about 80 °C and diluting to 250.00 mL. Compound 2 was prepared by the same procedure as compound 1, replacing Gd(ClO4)3 with Dy(ClO4)3: sodium acetate (273.0 mg, 2.0 mmol), N-acetyl-D-glucosamine (221.0 mg, 1.0 mmol), and Dy(ClO4)3 (4.0 mL, 4.0 mmol) in anhydrous ethanol (10 mL) and deionized water (5 mL), heated to about 80 °C, treated dropwise with aqueous NaOH (1.0 M) to incipient permanent precipitation, refluxed for 2 h, filtered, and crystallized by ambient evaporation.

reagents.amount: 4.0 mL of 1.0 mol L−1, 4.0 mmol (same procedure as 1)

synthesis.time: 2 h reflux; crystals after ambient evaporation
synthesis.vessel_or_method: open reflux in ethanol/water followed by ambient evaporation
synthesis.workup_and_crystallization: Same as compound 1: filtered and the filtrate evaporated under ambient conditions to give pale-yellow block crystals.

properties.summary: χMT is 125.12 cm3 K mol−1 at 300 K under 1000 Oe, close to 127.50 cm3 K mol−1 for nine uncoupled Dy3+ ions, and falls to 67.65 cm3 K mol−1 at 2 K. AC susceptibility (2.0–10.0 K) shows frequency-dependent out-of-phase signals without maxima at zero dc field because of quantum tunneling; maxima appear under a 10 kOe dc field, indicating single-molecule-magnet behavior. CD spectra in EtOH are shown without numerical optical data.
